scope: Read-only identity/hardware probes plus a Strata CUDA build on the SSH host named strix. Determines whether 12 GB VRAM is enforced and whether the 8 GB RTX 5070 Laptop GPU can build and launch the engine.

host.product: ASUSTeK COMPUTER INC. ROG Strix G16 G615LP_G615LP

limitation_finding.single_gpu: No hard VRAM minimum is enforced. setup.py gpu_problem() rejects architecture before Turing, but not a supported single GPU for low VRAM.
limitation_finding.warning: setup.py warns below 11 GB: Strata will run, but most experts stay on the CPU and it will be slow.
limitation_finding.multi_gpu: A card participating in a layer split must be at least SPLIT_MIN_VRAM_GB = 8 GB, with a 0.5 GB tolerance in gpu_problem().
limitation_finding.split_prompt_recommendation: SPLIT_PROMPT_VRAM_GB = 12 is a split-stage prompt-buffer recommendation, not the single-GPU requirement.
limitation_finding.docs: docs/INSTALL.md and docs/AI_SETUP.md state that a 12 GB card is recommended and an NVIDIA 8 GB card runs slowly. README.md compresses this to 12 GB or more and omits the 8 GB qualifier.

checks.result: Detected RTX 5070 Laptop GPU 8.0 GB, warned below 12 GB, and concluded: This PC can run Strata.
CUDA engine built 135/135 for sm_120 with CUDA 13.4 and g++-13; BUILD.json source hash 62eb4907c92a8cb7.
Binary resolves CUDA 13.4 runtime/cuBLAS libraries and prints help successfully.

non_claims: No model download, pack preparation, server start, inference request, output-quality check, or performance measurement was run.
A successful sm_120 build and --help launch do not establish stable runtime at 8 GB with a real model.
The idle PCIe width probe reported x8 of a possible x16; no load-time link measurement was made.
Ubuntu 26.04 is outside setup.py's automatic Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 CUDA install path; this build used the preinstalled system CUDA 13.4.
